newsitem.title: UK: Royal Dutch/Shell sees volatile oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Royal Dutch/Shell sees volatile oil prices.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group, one of the world's biggest companies, on Thursday reported an eight percent rise in third quarter net earnings, helped by a special credit, amid lower refining and marketing results.
Net earnings including extraordinary items rose to 1.201 billion pounds ($1.95 billion) from 1.117 billion, with the Anglo-Dutch oil giant saying it expected oil prices to remain volatile.
Without the 84 million pound special credit, net earnings fell seven percent to 1.117 billion pounds, coming in at the lower end of analysts' expectations.
Exploration and production earnings rose considerably, mainly due to strong crude oil prices, lower costs as well as higher production and more gas sales outside the U.S.
But industry-wide overcapicity continued to weigh on refining and marketing operations, which suffered from lower profit margins.
In addition, chemical earnings were substantially lower because of a difficult trading environment compared with favourable conditions a year ago. ($1=.6165 Pound)
